item.title: FCCC conducts targeted price checks on essential items amid drought concerns
item.description: The Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission (FCCC) is conducting targeted price surveys across retail outlets to protect consumers from unfair pricing of essential items during the current dry conditions. The FCCC says the monitoring is aimed at ensuring traders do not take advantage of increased demand for essential goods by imposing unfair price increases.
item.content:encoded:
The Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission (FCCC) is conducting targeted price surveys across retail outlets to protect consumers from unfair pricing of essential items during the current dry conditions.

The FCCC says the monitoring is aimed at ensuring traders do not take advantage of increased demand for essential goods by imposing unfair price increases.

They say the surveys are focusing on products that households may need, as they cope with water shortages and other challenges associated with the dry conditions.

These include bottled water, water filters, water pumps and accessories, generators, solar chargers, torches, lanterns, dust masks and candles.

The Commission says the monitoring is intended to prevent unfair pricing and anti-competitive practices while ensuring consumers are treated fairly.

They are reminding traders to comply with relevant pricing regulations and avoid taking advantage of consumers during this period.

The FCCC is also encouraging members of the public to remain vigilant when purchasing essential items and report any suspected unfair price increases.

They say consumer reports can help identify potential pricing concerns and support efforts to ensure compliance with the law.

Anyone who notices suspected unfair pricing can contact the FCCC through its toll-free number 1542, call 892 1991, or email helpdesk@fccc.gov.fj .

item.title: Kaloumaira says GCC records 94% support among iTaukei respondents for proposed constitution changes
item.description: The Great Council of Chiefs says around 94 percent of iTaukei respondents support proposed changes to the 2013 Constitution, following awareness consultations held in villages and communities. In a post in the iTaukei language, GCC Secretary Isoa Kaloumaira says the figures gathered through the Council's awareness consultations indicate that the support represents approximately 54 percent of Fiji'
item.content:encoded:
The Great Council of Chiefs says around 94 percent of iTaukei respondents support proposed changes to the 2013 Constitution, following awareness consultations held in villages and communities.

In a post in the iTaukei language, GCC Secretary Isoa Kaloumaira says the figures gathered through the Council's awareness consultations indicate that the support represents approximately 54 percent of Fiji's total population.

The total number of respondents is yet to be revealed.

Kaloumaira also says the Council has been actively involved in educating members of the public in villages and communities about the proposed constitutional changes to ensure people understand what is being proposed.

He also outlines the Council's current responsibilities and future plans, including its Strategic Intent, which will provide direction for the Council's operations and guide its engagement with other organisations.

Kaloumaira acknowledges the support and cooperation shown by traditional leaders and chiefs in the various areas visited during the consultations.

He says their involvement has been important in helping the Council carry out its awareness activities and reach communities.

The GCC Secretary also stresses the importance of ensuring that young people understand the Great Council of Chiefs, its role and the responsibilities it carries in relation to the iTaukei people.

He says it is important for the younger generation to be aware of the Council's work and understand its place in representing and addressing matters concerning the iTaukei community.
